newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Manning re-elected opposition leader in Trinidad.
newsitem.headline: Manning re-elected opposition leader in Trinidad.

text.p: Patrick Manning was re-elected political leader of the opposition People's National Movement in Trinidad on Sunday at the party's 34th annual convention.
According to elections officer, Hedwigde Bereaux, Manning polled 438 votes against 279 received by challenger Dr Keith Rowely.
Dr Linda Baboolal, an Indo-Trinidadian medical doctor, was elected chairman of the black-dominated party founded in 1956. She is the first women to hold the post.
Manning, now opposition leader, was prime minister for three years and 10 months. His slate of candidates was elected by a landslide for the 16 executive posts that were contested.
